methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 56 ENEC patients (39 surgical) with clear inclusion/exclusion and pre-specified OS/PFS endpoints, but the surgical vs non-surgical comparison is subject to unaddressed selection bias (Table I shows baseline differences in tumor length, thickness, cT/cN stage) and is acknowledged only briefly without matching or propensity adjustment. Statistical methods are appropriate in type (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, univariate/multivariate Cox with HRs and 95% CIs) but authors explicitly report no power analysis; biomarker-positive subgroups (5 BRAF+, 6 PD-L1+, 9 MiNEC-SCC) are too small for stable multivariate estimates, no multiplicity correction is described, and handling of missing data is not reported. IHC scoring used two independent pathologists with consensus adjudication and standard controls, strengthening the biomarker component.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Non-comparative single-center retrospective case series maps to Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is moderate: the question addresses a rare lethal malignancy lacking disease-specific guidelines, uses patient-relevant endpoints (OS/PFS), and replicates in a rare tumor the survival benefit of surgery and postoperative adjuvant therapy seen in other ENEC cohorts. The biomarker findings (PD-L1 15.4%, BRAF V600E 12.8%, enriched in the MiNEC-SCC subtype at 33.3%) have plausible translational implications for patient selection in checkpoint-inhibitor or targeted-therapy combinations but are not yet actionable given small numbers and absence of functional validation.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the applicable standard for this retrospective cohort. Most core items are present: setting, eligibility, patient-flow (Fig. 1), detailed IHC methodology including antibody catalog numbers and dilutions, statistical methods, baseline and outcome tables with HRs and CIs. Gaps: no protocol registration, no pre-specified primary outcome, no stated handling of missing data, no power calculation, limited confounding/selection-bias discussion. Data and code availability are weak — no data-availability statement, no repository deposit, no analytic code, and raw IHC images for several markers are explicitly unavailable, making reproducibility dependent on author request.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is primarily empirical and incremental. Authors claim first simultaneous assessment of BRAF V600E and PD-L1 in ENEC, but the introduction/discussion cite directly comparable prior PD-L1 work in ENEC (Yamashita, Huang, Xing) and BRAF mutation rates in GI neuroendocrine carcinoma (Dizdar, Idrees, Capdevila). No new assay, model, or hypothesis is introduced. The MiNEC-SCC enrichment observation rests on only 9 cases and is descriptive; prognostic findings replicate prior ENEC cohorts.

writing_presentation.justification: Well organized IMRaD structure; abstract is self-contained and numerically consistent with the body (BRAF V600E 12.8%, PD-L1 15.4%, 1-year OS/PFS 79.7/43.1%). Acronyms expanded on first use; Discussion contextualizes findings without recapitulating results. Minor issues: occasional awkward phrasing, one inconsistency in Table SIII numerator reporting for MiNEC-SCC PD-L1 positivity, and figure/table captions that lean on cross-references. Overall communicates effectively with only minor tightening needed.

key_strengths: Addresses a rare, understudied malignancy (esophageal neuroendocrine carcinoma) where new descriptive data are clinically useful
Patient-relevant endpoints (OS, PFS) with appropriate Kaplan-Meier and Cox modeling
Rigorous IHC methodology: two independent pathologists with consensus adjudication, documented antibody catalog/dilutions, standard positive and negative controls
Clear IMRaD writing with numerically consistent abstract and pre-specified endpoint definitions
key_concerns: Surgical vs non-surgical comparison subject to unaddressed selection bias; significant baseline differences in tumor length, thickness, and stage not adjusted via matching or propensity scoring
Biomarker-positive subgroups are too small (n=5-9) for stable multivariate estimation; no multiplicity correction across multiple subgroup analyses
No power analysis, no pre-registered protocol, no stated handling of missing data
Novelty is incremental — directly comparable prior PD-L1 and BRAF studies in ENEC and GI neuroendocrine carcinoma already cited; no new mechanism, assay, or hypothesis
Data and code availability absent; raw IHC images for several markers explicitly unavailable, limiting reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent but descriptive retrospective single-center cohort with incremental novelty, small biomarker subgroups, and weak reproducibility posture. Fits Tier 4 (IF < 4) oncology journals where descriptive series on rare tumors are routinely published; minor revisions would address the selection-bias framing and reporting-standard gaps.
